turns.content: ok so like... I said no to Tariq using my GPU node this afternoon and he literally muttered "not being a team player" under his breath and walked off 😬 and now I'm just sitting here like... was I actually being selfish?? my pipelines are literally running all weekend and the lab rules say I don't have to share but still... idk maybe I'm overthinking this

Okay, first: the fact that you're sitting here questioning yourself is kind of the tell. Actually-selfish people don't do that. They just say no and go get a snack.

Now the actual situation: you had jobs already running, they're running all weekend, and the lab explicitly says you don't have to give up your allocation. That's not a gray area, that's just... a no with receipts. "Team player" doesn't mean "drop your work whenever someone asks." It means not being a jerk about resources when it's *reasonable* to share, and interrupting a multi-day pipeline to hand over your node for an afternoon is not reasonable. He'd have said no in your position too.

The muttering is the part that stings, and yeah, it's a crappy move on his part. Passive-aggressive commentary under the breath is how people guilt you when they don't actually have a real argument. If he thought you were wrong, he could've said "hey, is there any window this weekend?" instead of walking off. That's on him, not you.

That said, two small things worth a thought, not because you did anything wrong but because it might make Monday less awkward:

- If there *is* a slot where your pipeline could pause or you could squeeze him in, offering it unprompted ("hey, node frees up Sunday night if you still need it") costs you nothing and quietly makes the "not a team player" thing look silly.
- If there isn't, you don't owe anything. Maybe a low-key "sorry I couldn't help earlier, jobs are locked in till Monday" if you run into him. Or nothing. Both are fine.

You're not overthinking it in the sense of being wrong, you're overthinking it in the sense that it's already resolved and your brain hasn't gotten the memo yet. Go do something that isn't replaying a mumbled sentence. 😅

ok yeah no I'm definitely not confronting him or bringing it up on Monday or emailing the PI or any of that 😬 I just wanna not make it weird y'know? like how do I coexist with him in the lab without apologizing or acting like I did something wrong

Totally fair, and the good news is "not making it weird" is mostly about doing *less*, not more.

The trick is to act like nothing happened, because from your side, nothing did. You made a normal call. So Monday you just... be normal. Say hi like you'd say hi to anyone. Ask if he saw whatever, complain about the coffee machine, whatever your usual lab small talk is. Don't avoid eye contact, don't go extra chirpy to compensate, don't hover. The more you treat it as a non-event, the faster it becomes one.

A few small things that help:

- **Don't bring up the node at all.** No "sorry about Friday," no "hope you found a machine." Any mention of it reopens the thing you want closed. If *he* brings it up, keep it short and neutral: "yeah, jobs were locked in all weekend" and move on. No explaining, no justifying.
- **Let the silence sit if he's cool for a bit.** Some people need a day to get over being told no. If he's a little clipped Monday, that's his weather, not yours. Don't chase it.
- **Be normal-nice, not extra-nice.** Extra-nice reads as guilt. You're going for "colleague I have no beef with," not "colleague I'm trying to win back."
- **If sharing ever does make sense later**, just do it like a regular person would. Not as a peace offering, just as the thing you'd do anyway. That quietly makes the "team player" comment age badly without you saying a word.

Odds are decent he's already half forgotten it and was just annoyed in the moment because his afternoon plan fell through. You're the one who took it home. So the coexistence plan is basically: don't perform anything, let it evaporate, and go back to being the person who does their work and isn't weird about it. 🙂

ughhh thank you for that 😅 seriously. ok so like... I know I said I'm not gonna escalate or whatever but hypothetically... if someone *did* want to report a senior labmate for pulling the "team player" card... is that even a thing? or is it just normal lab grumbling I should ignore

Hypothetically? 😄 Sure, let's play it out.

One muttered "not a team player" after being told no is, in the grand hierarchy of lab nonsense, pretty firmly in the *grumbling* tier. It's petty, it's annoying, but if you took it to a PI or an ombudsperson, the likely response would be a sympathetic nod and "yeah, people say dumb things when they're frustrated." Nobody's writing anyone up for a mumble. Reporting it would probably cost you more socially than it'd cost him.

Where it *does* become a thing is if it stops being a one-off:

- **It turns into a pattern.** Repeated guilt-tripping, snide comments in front of others, making you the "difficult one" in group settings.
- **He uses his seniority.** Pressure like "as the senior person I'm telling you to give it up," or leaning on his standing to get around the lab rules.
- **It affects your actual work.** Retaliation, being cut out of things, weird friction on shared projects, your allocation mysteriously getting questioned.
- **Anything that crosses into harassment territory**, which this isn't, but that's the bright line.

At that point you'd go to the PI (or lab manager, or whoever handles this) not with "he said a mean thing," but with "there's an ongoing pattern about resource sharing and it's making things tense, can we clarify expectations." That framing is about the *lab functioning*, not about him being a jerk, and it gets taken seriously.

For now, the thing worth doing is the boring thing: keep a mental note. If it happens once, it's a mood. If it happens three times in a month, it's a data point, and you'll be glad you remembered the dates. That's not escalating, that's just paying attention.

But honestly your instinct earlier was right. This one's a "let it evaporate" situation. Save your hypothetical reporting energy for the version of Tariq who does this repeatedly. 🙂

ok yeah no that all makes sense 😅 I'm definitely not reporting anything. just wanted to check if I was being dumb for letting it bug me. I'll just let it be and not make it weird on Monday. thanks for talking me down lol

Not dumb at all. Getting a passive-aggressive mutter aimed at you when you did nothing wrong is *supposed* to be a little irritating, that's just your brain doing its "wait, was that fair?" check. You ran the check, it came back clean, you're good.

Enjoy the weekend while your pipelines do their thing, and Monday will be a lot more boring than your Friday-evening brain is predicting. 🙂
yeah you're right lol. I think I just needed to hear someone say it's fine. I'll let it go and just be normal Monday. thanks again 😅
Anytime. 🙂 Go enjoy the weekend, and let those pipelines earn their keep. Monday's gonna be a total non-event.
